summary: Load `clusters.yaml` with `podman cp clusters.yaml automation-dashboard-web:/tmp` and `podman exec -it automation-dashboard-web /venv/bin/python manage.py setclusters /tmp/clusters.yaml`; tokens rotate internally, so get current ones with `manage.py getclusters --decrypt` before re-running setclusters.
questions: How do I load clusters.yaml into automation dashboard?
How do I get the current tokens from automation dashboard?

answer_card.title: Load cluster config into automation dashboard
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
podman cp clusters.yaml automation-dashboard-web:/tmp
podman exec -it automation-dashboard-web /venv/bin/python manage.py setclusters /tmp/clusters.yaml
```
The dashboard rotates tokens internally but does not update your local file. Before re-running `setclusters`, export the current ones:
```bash
podman exec -it automation-dashboard-web /venv/bin/python manage.py getclusters --decrypt > clusters_current.yaml
```
